thread:
alex_sales: Hey team — large deal with FinHealth CN. They require strict data residency: all inference + logs must remain in mainland CN, no cross-border egress allowed. Can we confirm: 1) list of CN-region subprocessors, 2) routing policy options (hard region pin vs. soft failover), 3) is Private/VPC or Dedicated needed to meet their legal ask, and 4) ballpark pricing for a 3-month POC with ~200 req/s sustained?

mia_se: +1 — key questions for scoping. Quick answers: we have a CN-hosted footprint (partnered region) but there are two deployment models that matter: Private (customer VPC/on-prem) and Dedicated (reserved capacity in CN partner). Private = strongest compliance (no shared infra), Dedicated = shared infra but can be isolated tenant-level with contractual guarantees.

mia_se: For subprocessors: I can pull the latest export, but note we use a local cloud partner + an audit-backed caching layer. Need to confirm exact partner names we list in legal for CN.

priya_legal: Please send the customer's security questionnaire. We will need to map subprocessors, data flow, and CA/B compliance. For CN customers we usually include: local cloud partner, telemetry processor (audit logs), and backup storage partner. Will validate whether we can represent them by role or must list legal entity names.

alex_sales: Added the SQ in thread. deploy-bot: uploaded security_questionnaire_FinHealthCN.pdf

cheng_se: Quick routing policy note — we support three rough modes: 
- pin: route only to CN-region replicas (no cross-border)
- prefer: try CN first, fallback to global if capacity exceeded
- failover-with-consent: failover only if customer toggles opt-in

Example policy snippet the customer asked for (they want to embed in their design doc):
```
routing: 
  region_preference: cn-mainland
  fallback: none  # no fallback allowed for residency-sensitive tenants
```

tomas_infra: Implementation/ops constraints: If they require zero egress under all failure modes, Private/VPC is the safest. Dedicated in a partner zone can meet it if we disable cross-region networking and sign appropriate addenda, but we must validate partner subprocessor controls. Also note: KV-cache snapshots and model artifact updates — we need an approved upload path (s3-like) inside CN.

mia_se: POC scope suggestion: 12 GPU hours/day average, 200 req/s, <150ms p95. For a 3-month POC we usually quote: 
- Dedicated (CN partner): ballpark commit range 25-60k USD/month (depends on instance mix and network egress configs)
- Private (VPC/on-prem): implementation + ops uplift, one-time onboarding fee + infra cost (high variance).

alex_sales: Can you turn the Dedicated ballpark into a formal quote? The procurement team will need line items: compute, storage, data egress (should be 0 if pinned), monitoring retention. Also they asked about certs: do we have SOC/ISO equivalents for the CN partner?

tomas_infra: We have attestations for the CN partner, but not full SOC 2 in the same form — legal will need to sign region-specific exhibits. I'll pull the partner compliance pack.

priya_legal: I'll prep a redlined exhibit for Mainland CN and confirm whether we can list entity names in the subprocessor appendix. Also need to answer questions about key management: we offer customer-managed keys (KMS) for Private; for Dedicated we can provide an HSM-backed option via partner — will confirm exact key lifecycle.

alex_sales: Timeline: the customer wants POC to start in 3 weeks. Is that feasible? What are blockers?

mia_se: Blockers: partner paperwork (subprocessor addendum), network peering certs, and if Private is chosen — on-prem install window. If Dedicated, capacity reservation lead time is ~10 business days after contract. So 3 weeks feasible if we rush approvals.

cheng_se: Action items: 
- mia_se: prepare Dedicated vs Private playbook + checklist for CN (network certs, KMS options, subprocessor list)
- tomas_infra: fetch partner compliance pack and confirm egress controls + artifact update path
- priya_legal: prepare subprocessor appendix draft and review KMS/HSM language
- alex_sales: collect customer's legal contact and confirm POC start date window

alex_sales: I'll get their procurement contact this afternoon and share the security questionnaire filled with Prod answers. Any objections to sharing the sample routing policy and the Dedicated ballpark with customer?

priya_legal: share with watermark and note "subject to final compliance review". No raw partner certs until NDA.

mia_se: I'll draft the CN playbook and ballpark quote today, upload by EOD.

tomas_infra: FYI — linking internal subprocessors doc: https://internal.redwood/sops/subprocessors (private link). I'll DM access to folks who need it.

alex_sales: Thanks all — will post customer's procurement contact once I have it. :thumbsup:
